page.layout: One text column with two inline figures (a pentagram and a hexagon) set into the text; no marginal notes. Head: page number and running head. Below the figures a centred chapter heading, then one paragraph.

main_text.p: Nobilissima est & celeberrima hæc figura, quæ dicitur ὑγίεια id est sanitas Pythagoræ, quia Pythagoras hanc figuram in schola delectat° asscribebat singulis prominentibus angulis quinque, literas constituentes vocem ὑγίεια: Germani vocant eam Trudenfuß quia Sacerdotes veteres Germanorum siue Gallorum vocabantur Druidæ & dicuntur gestasse calceos huius figuræ.

6. Hexagoni siue Sexanguli etiam facilis est constructio: primo enim ducitur circulus; deinde in isto circulo cætera omnia ita eriguntur, vt in illo Pentagono Pythagorico b.a.e.d.c. modo à c & d.ad inferiore circuli parte mediam (exempli gratia) ad F tales duæ lineæ ducantur, quales ductæ sunt à b & e ad angulum a, vt ad oculum apparet ex figura illa pentagonali Pythagorica, quam paulo ante depinximus, vel ex hac.

page.notes: Figure labels (pentagram: a, b, c, d, e, F; hexagon: a, b, c, d, e, F, and numerals 1 to 6) are part of the drawings and are not transcribed as text. The Greek word ὑγίεια is set in the printed figure caption; the glyphs were read as printed. The drop-cap H of the final paragraph is read as H followed by Actenus. The word "Incompletā" has a tilde over the a as printed.
